components.note: 夕 (evening) — the left part, the time-of-day family as in 夜, 多, 梦. Memory aid: things done at night are outside the ordinary.
卜 (divination) — Dictionary story: night 夕 divination 卜, strange and 'outside'. A hedged mnemonic: 外面 outside, 另外 in addition.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过 pass, 进 enter, 送 send; to meet is to cross paths.
禺 (yú) is close to yù; same part in 愚 yú and 偶 ǒu.

example.hanzi: 小说描写了一段复杂的外遇。
example.pinyin: xiǎoshuō miáoxiě le yí duàn fùzá de wàiyù.
example.english: The novel depicts a complicated affair.
example.fact: Emperor penguins are famously monogamous for a single breeding season but re-pair with a different partner nearly every year. Studies tracking banded birds found fewer than 15% of pairs reunite for a second season, despite the species' reputation for devotion.

examples.hanzi: 他因为外遇而和妻子离婚了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīnwèi wàiyù ér hé qīzi líhūn le.
examples.english: He divorced his wife because of an affair.

examples.hanzi: 这部电视剧讲的是一个家庭因外遇而破裂的故事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànshìjù jiǎng de shì yí gè jiātíng yīn wàiyù ér pòliè de gùshi.
examples.english: This TV series tells the story of a family broken apart by an affair.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; sand grains are tiny bits washed by water.
少 (shǎo) — near sound — 沙 is shā; 少 also sounds out 炒 chǎo and 纱 shā.
扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 推, 拿; 拉 is to pull.
立 (lì) hints at the sound: 拉 lā is close, as in 垃 lā.

example.hanzi: 她午餐只吃了一份沙拉。
example.pinyin: tā wǔcān zhǐ chī le yí fèn shālā.
example.english: She only ate a salad for lunch.
example.fact: The Caesar salad wasn't invented in Rome or by a chef named Caesar. It was created in 1924 by Italian-American restaurateur Caesar Cardini in Tijuana, Mexico, reportedly improvised from limited ingredients during a busy Fourth of July weekend.

examples.hanzi: 我想点一份水果沙拉。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng diǎn yí fèn shuǐguǒ shālā.
examples.english: I'd like to order a fruit salad.

examples.hanzi: 这家餐厅的沙拉酱特别好吃。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de shālājiàng tèbié hǎochī.
examples.english: The salad dressing at this restaurant is especially delicious.

components.note: 辶 (movement) — marks walking and roads, as in 过, 进, 送; 遵 is to follow a path.
尊 (zūn) gives the sound exactly: 遵 zūn, and also gives the sense of honouring.
口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: an order is spoken.
令 (lìng, order) is a close sound clue for mìng; 令 also in 领 lǐng, 冷 lěng and 零 líng.

example.hanzi: 士兵回答道:"遵命,长官!"
example.pinyin: shìbīng huídá dào: "zūnmìng, zhǎngguān!"
example.english: The soldier replied, "Yes sir, as ordered!"
example.fact: The rigid chain-of-command culture in military organizations traces back to Prussian army reforms of the early 1800s. Those reforms formalized standardized ranks, drills, and staff systems that most modern militaries, including NATO forces, still structurally resemble today.

examples.hanzi: “去把窗户关上。”“遵命！”
examples.pinyin: “Qù bǎ chuānghu guān shàng.” “Zūnmìng!”
examples.english: “Go close the window.” “Yes, sir!”

examples.hanzi: 他笑着说：“遵命，老板！”
examples.pinyin: Tā xiàozhe shuō: “Zūnmìng, lǎobǎn!”
examples.english: He said with a smile, “As you wish, boss!”

components.note: 主 (master, host) — a lamp with a flame on top; a lamp stand was the centre of the room. 主 also sounds out 注 zhù, 住 zhù and 柱 zhù.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: holding on.
寺 (sì) is a loose sound clue for chí; 寺 also in 诗 shī, 待 dài, 特 tè and 等 děng.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 她是一名很受欢迎的电视节目主持人。
example.pinyin: tā shì yì míng hěn shòu huānyíng de diànshì jiémù zhǔchírén.
example.english: She is a very popular TV show host.
example.fact: Johnny Carson hosted NBC's "The Tonight Show" for nearly 30 years, from 1962 to 1992, and at his peak commanded roughly 17 million viewers a night. No single late-night host has matched that scale of nightly reach since television fragmented across cable and streaming.

examples.hanzi: 晚会的主持人讲话很幽默。
examples.pinyin: Wǎnhuì de zhǔchírén jiǎnghuà hěn yōumò.
examples.english: The host of the evening party speaks humorously.

examples.hanzi: 他想当一名广播电台的主持人。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng dāng yì míng guǎngbō diàntái de zhǔchírén.
examples.english: He wants to be a radio presenter.

components.note: 手 (hand) — the bottom 手 is a hand — 举 is lifting with the hands, as in 举行.
力 (strength) — effort and motion, as in 办, 助, 努. The part 云 stands in for 重 in the traditional 動, which was the sound clue.

example.hanzi: 他的这个举动让所有人感到惊讶。
example.pinyin: tā de zhège jǔdòng ràng suǒyǒu rén gǎndào jīngyà.
example.english: This action of his surprised everyone.
example.fact: Jane Goodall's 1960s observations of chimpanzees using grass stems to fish termites out of mounds were among the first documented cases of tool use by non-human animals. The discovery forced scientists to redefine what separates humans from other species.

examples.hanzi: 他突然的举动吓了大家一跳。
examples.pinyin: Tā tūrán de jǔdòng xià le dàjiā yí tiào.
examples.english: His sudden action gave everyone a start.

examples.hanzi: 他这个举动很不礼貌。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhège jǔdòng hěn bù lǐmào.
examples.english: This action of his is very impolite.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person falling over; marks people and their actions, as in 你, 做.
到 (dào) gives the sound: 倒 is dǎo (fall) or dào (upside down).
攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action, here counting; as in 教, 放.
娄 (lóu) — loose hint — 数 is shù; 娄 also sounds out 楼 lóu.

example.hanzi: 人群一起倒数迎接新年。
example.pinyin: rénqún yìqǐ dàoshǔ yíngjiē xīnnián.
example.english: The crowd counted down together to welcome the new year.
example.fact: NASA's launch countdown tradition is partly credited to the 1929 German science-fiction film "Frau im Mond" (Woman in the Moon). Its director, Fritz Lang, added the countdown purely for dramatic suspense, and the convention stuck for real rocket launches decades later.

examples.hanzi: 他在班上考了倒数第三名。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài bān shàng kǎo le dàoshǔ dì-sān míng.
examples.english: He came third from the bottom in the class.

examples.hanzi: 火箭发射前，大家开始倒数十秒。
examples.pinyin: Huǒjiàn fāshè qián, dàjiā kāishǐ dàoshǔ shí miǎo.
examples.english: Before the rocket launched, everyone began the ten-second countdown.

meanings: abbr. for 費拉德爾菲亞|费拉德尔菲亚[Fei4 la1 de2 er3 fei1 ya4]

components.note: 贝 (cowry shell, money) — money and trade: 财, 货, 买, 贵; 费 is a cost or fee.
弗 (fú) is close to fèi; same part in 沸 fèi.
土 (earth) — ground and land: 地, 场, 块; city walls were made of earth.
成 (chéng) sounds exactly like 城; also in 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng.

example.hanzi: 独立宣言是在费城签署的。
example.pinyin: Dúlì Xuānyán shì zài Fèichéng qiānshǔ de.
example.english: The Declaration of Independence was signed in Philadelphia.
example.fact: Philadelphia's Liberty Bell, a symbol of American independence, has been cracked since at least 1846. The flaw reportedly worsened during a test ring for George Washington's birthday, and the bell has not been rung since for fear of causing further damage.

examples.hanzi: 费城是美国历史上很重要的城市。
examples.pinyin: Fèichéng shì Měiguó lìshǐ shàng hěn zhòngyào de chéngshì.
examples.english: Philadelphia is a very important city in American history.

examples.hanzi: 我们下个月坐火车去费城。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xià gè yuè zuò huǒchē qù Fèichéng.
examples.english: Next month we are taking the train to Philadelphia.

components.note: 手 (hand) — over 目 (eye): a hand shading the eyes to look into the distance. 目 marks seeing words, as in 眼, 睡.
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.hanzi: 雾太大了,我们看不到山顶。
example.pinyin: wù tài dà le, wǒmen kànbudào shāndǐng.
example.english: The fog is too thick; we can't see the mountain peak.
example.fact: Mount Everest's summit is shrouded in cloud or storm for most of the year. Climbers have only a narrow weather window, usually in May, when jet-stream winds temporarily shift and expose the peak long enough for a safe summit attempt.

examples.hanzi: 前面的人太高了，我看不到舞台。
examples.pinyin: Qiánmiàn de rén tài gāo le, wǒ kàn bu dào wǔtái.
examples.english: The person in front is too tall; I can't see the stage.

examples.hanzi: 城市里晚上几乎看不到星星。
examples.pinyin: Chéngshì lǐ wǎnshang jīhū kàn bu dào xīngxing.
examples.english: You can hardly see stars at night in the city.

meanings: various birds of the family Columbidae

components.note: 鸟 (bird) — marks birds, as in 鸭 duck, 鸡 chicken, 鹅 goose.
合 (hé) is only a loose sound clue — 鸽 is gē; 合 also sounds out 哈 hā and 给 gěi.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 广场上有很多鸽子。
example.pinyin: guǎngchǎng shàng yǒu hěn duō gēzi.
example.english: There are many pigeons in the square.
example.fact: Homing pigeons carried messages across enemy lines in both World Wars. One bird named Cher Ami saved nearly 200 American soldiers in 1918 by delivering a critical message despite being shot through the breast and losing a leg during the flight.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在广场上喂鸽子。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài guǎngchǎng shàng wèi gēzi.
examples.english: The children are feeding pigeons in the square.

examples.hanzi: 爷爷在楼顶养了几只鸽子。
examples.pinyin: Yéye zài lóudǐng yǎng le jǐ zhī gēzi.
examples.english: Grandpa keeps a few pigeons on the roof.

components.note: 戈 (halberd) — weapons, as in 战 war and 成; the traditional 戲 was a play or contest.
刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife), as in 到, 别, 利; 剧 first meant to cut deeply, then intense and drama.
居 (jū) — near sound — 剧 is jù; 居 also sounds out 据 jù.

example.hanzi: 这部戏剧改编自莎士比亚的作品。
example.pinyin: zhè bù xìjù gǎibiān zì Shāshìbǐyà de zuòpǐn.
example.english: This drama is adapted from a work by Shakespeare.
example.fact: Shakespeare's Globe Theatre in London could hold roughly 3,000 spectators, many of them "groundlings" who paid just a penny to stand in the open-air yard. The original building burned down in 1613 after a stage cannon set the thatched roof alight.

examples.hanzi: 她从小就对戏剧很感兴趣。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù duì xìjù hěn gǎn xìngqù.
examples.english: She has been interested in drama since childhood.

examples.hanzi: 他后来选择了戏剧专业。
examples.pinyin: Tā hòulái xuǎnzé le xìjù zhuānyè.
examples.english: He later chose to major in drama.

components.note: 小 (small) — a 小 with a stroke taken off: not much. 少 also gives sound to 沙 shā, 抄 chāo and 炒 chǎo.
女 (woman) — a person kneeling with arms crossed; as a radical it heads many female and family words: 妈, 好, 姐.

example.hanzi: 那位少女梦想成为一名科学家。
example.pinyin: nà wèi shàonǚ mèngxiǎng chéngwéi yì míng kēxuéjiā.
example.english: That young girl dreams of becoming a scientist.
example.fact: Marie Curie became the first person ever to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences — physics in 1903 and chemistry in 1911. She conducted much of her early radioactivity research in a converted shed with no proper ventilation, unaware of the health risks.

examples.hanzi: 这个少女的笑容很甜。
examples.pinyin: Zhège shàonǚ de xiàoróng hěn tián.
examples.english: This young girl has a sweet smile.

examples.hanzi: 那是一个关于少女和小狗的童话。
examples.pinyin: Nà shì yí gè guānyú shàonǚ hé xiǎo gǒu de tónghuà.
examples.english: That is a fairy tale about a girl and a puppy.

components.note: 京 (jīng, high mound, capital) is a loose sound clue for jiù; going up to a high place fits 就 "to approach, to go to".
⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo, as in 笔 pen, 等 wait, 第: counting rods were once bamboo.
具 (jù, tool) — here the lower part shows hands holding the counting tools.

example.hanzi: 就算下雨,比赛也会照常进行。
example.pinyin: jiùsuàn xiàyǔ, bǐsài yě huì zhàocháng jìnxíng.
example.english: Even if it rains, the match will go on as scheduled.
example.fact: Wimbledon didn't install a retractable roof over Centre Court until 2009, after decades of rain delays. The tournament's grass courts are reseeded and closely monitored every year, since natural turf reacts unpredictably to even brief periods of wet weather.

examples.hanzi: 就算你不喜欢，也要试一试。
examples.pinyin: Jiùsuàn nǐ bù xǐhuan, yě yào shì yi shì.
examples.english: Even if you don't like it, you should give it a try.

examples.hanzi: 就算再累，他也坚持跑完了全程。
examples.pinyin: Jiùsuàn zài lèi, tā yě jiānchí pǎo wán le quánchéng.
examples.english: Even though he was tired, he kept going until he finished the whole course.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — hills and places: 院, 阳, 陆; 队 is a group of people gathered together.

example.hanzi: 一支小队负责搜救失踪的登山者。
example.pinyin: yì zhī xiǎoduì fùzé sōujiù shīzōng de dēngshānzhě.
example.english: A small team was responsible for rescuing the missing climber.
example.fact: Mountain rescue dogs can search an area the size of several football fields in about 30 minutes, a task that could take a human search team hours. Their sense of smell is estimated to be tens of thousands of times more sensitive than a human's.

examples.hanzi: 我们的小队有五个人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de xiǎoduì yǒu wǔ gè rén.
examples.english: Our squad has five people.

examples.hanzi: 老师把全班分成了四个小队。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī bǎ quán bān fēnchéng le sì gè xiǎoduì.
examples.english: The teacher divided the whole class into four small teams.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 执 is to hold or grasp, then carry out, as in 执行.
灬 (fire) — fire and heat, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 黑 black: light shining.
昭 (zhāo) is a close sound clue for zhào; 昭 itself means bright.

example.hanzi: 他刚拿到驾驶执照。
example.pinyin: tā gāng nádào jiàshǐ zhízhào.
example.english: He just got his driver's license.
example.fact: The world's first driving license law was introduced in France in 1893, requiring drivers to pass a technical exam and pledge not to endanger pedestrians. That came decades before most countries required any test at all to legally operate a motor vehicle.

examples.hanzi: 开餐馆需要有营业执照。
examples.pinyin: Kāi cānguǎn xūyào yǒu yíngyè zhízhào.
examples.english: You need a business license to open a restaurant.

examples.hanzi: 他的驾驶执照下个月到期。
examples.pinyin: Tā de jiàshǐ zhízhào xià gè yuè dàoqī.
examples.english: His driver's license expires next month.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 保 oldest form shows a person carrying a child on the back, so to protect.
呆 here is the old child shape 子 beside the person, a picture of keeping safe.
钅 (metal, simplified 金) — metal radical; 镖 is a metal dart, as in 钱 money, 铁 iron, 钟 bell.
票 (piào) shares the rhyme with biāo; it also sounds out 飘 piāo and 漂 piāo/piào.

example.hanzi: 那位明星有三名保镖跟随。
example.pinyin: nà wèi míngxīng yǒu sān míng bǎobiāo gēnsuí.
example.english: That celebrity is followed by three bodyguards.
example.fact: The U.S. Secret Service originally had nothing to do with presidential protection — it was founded in 1865 primarily to fight the widespread counterfeiting of currency. It only began guarding presidents full-time after President McKinley's assassination in 1901.

examples.hanzi: 总裁出门的时候都带着保镖。
examples.pinyin: Zǒngcái chūmén de shíhou dōu dàizhe bǎobiāo.
examples.english: The CEO always takes bodyguards when going out.

examples.hanzi: 他在电影里演了一个保镖。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài diànyǐng lǐ yǎn le yí gè bǎobiāo.
examples.english: He played a bodyguard in the movie.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — 灬 is fire at the bottom, as in 点, 照, 熟; 热 is heat.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 给, 组; 线 is thread or line.
戋 (jiān) is a loose sound clue; same part in 浅 qiǎn, 钱 qián and 残 cán.

example.hanzi: 请拨打客服热线咨询问题。
example.pinyin: qǐng bōdǎ kèfú rèxiàn zīxún wèntí.
example.english: Please call the customer service hotline with any questions.
example.fact: The "red telephone" hotline between Washington and Moscow, established in 1963 after the Cuban Missile Crisis, was never actually a phone at first. It was a teletype machine, chosen because typed messages left an unambiguous record to prevent dangerous mistranslation during a crisis.

examples.hanzi: 你可以拨打投诉热线反映问题。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ bōdǎ tóusù rèxiàn fǎnyìng wèntí.
examples.english: You can call the complaint hotline to report the problem.

examples.hanzi: 这个节目开通了听众热线。
examples.pinyin: Zhège jiémù kāitōng le tīngzhòng rèxiàn.
examples.english: This program has opened a hotline for listeners.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 推, 按; 抗 is to resist or hold off.
亢 (kàng) gives the sound exactly: 抗 kàng, also in 炕 kàng.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and language: 说 say, 请 ask, 话 speech; 议 is to discuss.
义 (yì) sounds exactly like 议; same part in 仪 yí and 蚁 yǐ.

example.hanzi: 数千人走上街头抗议新法案。
example.pinyin: shùqiān rén zǒushàng jiētóu kàngyì xīn fǎ'àn.
example.english: Thousands of people took to the streets to protest the new bill.
example.fact: The 1773 Boston Tea Party, one of history's most famous protests, saw colonists dump an estimated 92,000 pounds of tea into Boston Harbor. Its cleanup value in today's currency would run into the millions of dollars.

examples.hanzi: 居民们向政府提出了抗议。
examples.pinyin: Jūmínmen xiàng zhèngfǔ tíchū le kàngyì.
examples.english: The residents lodged a protest with the government.

examples.hanzi: 学生们抗议学校提高学费。
examples.pinyin: Xuéshengmen kàngyì xuéxiào tígāo xuéfèi.
examples.english: The students protested against the school raising tuition.

components.note: 大 (big) — the top. 奈 comes from 柰 (a crabapple 木 + 示); the sense 'how, to endure' is borrowed, as in 无奈 helpless, 奈何 what can be done.
示 (altar, to show) — the bottom; its 礻 form is in 神 spirit, 礼 ritual. Here it is just the visible part; the meaning is borrowed from the sound.

example.hanzi: 他无奈地笑了笑。
example.pinyin: Tā wúnài de xiào le xiào.
example.english: He smiled helplessly.
example.fact: 奈 is almost never used alone. Key forms are 无奈 (helpless) and 无可奈何 (nothing to be done), plus 奈何 ("what can be done"). In foreign names it gives the sound, as in 奈良 (Nara) and 奈飞 (Netflix).

examples.hanzi: 我对他没有办法,真是无可奈何。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì tā méiyǒu bànfǎ, zhēn shì wúkě nàihé.
examples.english: I can do nothing about him; I'm helpless.

examples.hanzi: 他很无奈,只好重新来过。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn wúnài, zhǐhǎo chóngxīn lái guò.
examples.english: He felt helpless and had to start over.

components.note: 童 (child) — as a sound unit, 童 also appears in 瞳 tóng and 撞 zhuàng; the character itself means child, as in 儿童.

example.hanzi: 这个儿童乐园很受欢迎。
example.pinyin: Zhège értóng lèyuán hěn shòu huānyíng.
example.english: This children's playground is very popular.
example.fact: 童 is mostly bound: 儿童 (children), 童年 (childhood), 童话 (fairy tale), 童装 (children's clothes). In classical Chinese 童 could also mean a young servant boy before it settled on "child."

examples.hanzi: 他有一个快乐的童年。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu yí ge kuàilè de tóngnián.
examples.english: He had a happy childhood.

examples.hanzi: 这本童话书很有趣。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn tónghuà shū hěn yǒuqù.
examples.english: This fairy tale book is very interesting.

components.note: 车 (chariot) — war chariots drawn up in a circle (the top part shows the enclosure): an army camp, hence military.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 他退伍后仍以曾是军人为荣。
example.pinyin: tā tuìwǔ hòu réng yǐ céng shì jūnrén wéi róng.
example.english: After discharge he was still proud to have been a soldier.
example.fact: The Terracotta Army, buried near Xi'an around 210 BC to guard China's first emperor in the afterlife, contains over 8,000 life-sized soldier statues. Each has individually sculpted facial features, and no two figures discovered so far are identical.

examples.hanzi: 他的爸爸是一名军人。
examples.pinyin: Tā de bàba shì yì míng jūnrén.
examples.english: His father is a soldier.

examples.hanzi: 军人要遵守严格的纪律。
examples.pinyin: Jūnrén yào zūnshǒu yángé de jìlǜ.
examples.english: Military personnel must follow strict discipline.

components.note: 周 (zhōu) also lends its sound to 调 diào/tiáo, 稠 chóu, 绸 chóu and 凋 diāo.
年 (year) — first drawn as a person carrying harvested grain: one harvest per year. Seen in 今年, 去年, 年轻.

example.hanzi: 公司即将迎来成立十周年。
example.pinyin: gōngsī jíjiāng yínglái chénglì shí zhōunián.
example.english: The company is about to celebrate its tenth anniversary.
example.fact: The Eiffel Tower was originally built as a temporary structure for the 1889 World's Fair, marking the 100th anniversary of the French Revolution. It was slated for demolition after 20 years but was saved because of its usefulness as a radio transmission tower.

examples.hanzi: 今天是我们结婚五周年。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān shì wǒmen jiéhūn wǔ zhōunián.
examples.english: Today is our fifth wedding anniversary.

examples.hanzi: 学校举行了建校一百周年庆典。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào jǔxíng le jiànxiào yì bǎi zhōunián qìngdiǎn.
examples.english: The school held a celebration for its hundredth anniversary.

components.note: 身 (body) — a person's body with a rounded belly. As a radical it marks body words: 躺 lie down, 躲 hide, 躯 body.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 份 is a person's portion or share.
分 (fēn) is a near sound match for fèn; also 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢: to prove by saying.
正 (zhèng) gives the exact sound; 正 also in 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 办理业务需要出示身份证。
example.pinyin: bànlǐ yèwù xūyào chūshì shēnfènzhèng.
example.english: You need to show your ID card to handle this business.
example.fact: Estonia issues a mandatory national ID card that doubles as a digital signature key, letting citizens vote, file taxes, and sign legal contracts entirely online. Over 99% of Estonia's public services have been available digitally since the early 2000s.

examples.hanzi: 进考场必须带身份证。
examples.pinyin: Jìn kǎochǎng bìxū dài shēnfènzhèng.
examples.english: You must bring your ID card to enter the exam hall.

examples.hanzi: 我的身份证丢了，要去补办。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shēnfènzhèng diū le, yào qù bǔbàn.
examples.english: I lost my ID card and need to get a replacement.

components.note: 氵 (water, 三点水) — marks water and liquids; 沟 is a ditch or channel, as in 河 river, 海 sea.
勾 (gōu) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 钩 gōu (hook) and 构 gòu.
辶 (walk) — movement and roads, as in 过, 近, 送: a way through.
甬 (yǒng) is a close sound clue for tōng; 甬 also in 痛 tòng, 桶 tǒng and 勇 yǒng.

example.hanzi: 良好的沟通可以避免很多误会。
example.pinyin: liánghǎo de gōutōng kěyǐ bìmiǎn hěn duō wùhuì.
example.english: Good communication can avoid a lot of misunderstandings.
example.fact: Honeybees communicate the direction and distance of food sources through a "waggle dance," encoding the sun's position and flight distance in the angle and duration of their movements. It is a symbolic communication system unusually sophisticated for an insect.

examples.hanzi: 夫妻之间要多沟通。
examples.pinyin: Fūqī zhījiān yào duō gōutōng.
examples.english: Couples should communicate more.

examples.hanzi: 我们需要和对方沟通一下。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xūyào hé duìfāng gōutōng yíxià.
examples.english: We need to communicate with the other side.

components.note: 旅 (travel) — a flag with people gathered under it: a troop on the march, then travellers on a journey.
氵 (water) — water and swimming, as in 河, 海, 泳: swimming and drifting.
斿 (yóu) gives the exact sound: a flag with streamers that floats freely.

example.hanzi: 暑假我们打算去云南旅游。
example.pinyin: shǔjià wǒmen dǎsuàn qù Yúnnán lǚyóu.
example.english: We plan to travel to Yunnan for summer vacation.
example.fact: Tourism now accounts for roughly 10% of global GDP and one in ten jobs worldwide. The industry ground to a near-total halt in 2020, when international arrivals fell by about 74%, the sharpest single-year drop ever recorded.

examples.hanzi: 我最喜欢去海边旅游。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan qù hǎibiān lǚyóu.
examples.english: I like traveling to the seaside the most.

examples.hanzi: 这个城市的旅游业很发达。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì de lǚyóuyè hěn fādá.
examples.english: This city's tourism industry is very developed.

components.note: 亻 (person) — a person leaning to one side; also in 他 he, 们 plural.
扁 (biǎn) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 篇 piān and 遍 biàn.

example.hanzi: 我越不想去，他偏偏要我去。
example.pinyin: Wǒ yuè bù xiǎng qù, tā piānpiān yào wǒ qù.
example.english: The less I wanted to go, the more he insisted that I go.
example.fact: 偏 means leaning to one side, so 偏心 is favoritism and 偏见 is prejudice. The adverb 偏偏 expresses "of all things" or "stubbornly," often with annoyance. 偏旁 is also the term for a character's component.

examples.hanzi: 这个房间偏小。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fángjiān piān xiǎo.
examples.english: This room is a bit small.

examples.hanzi: 你偏偏不听我的话。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ piānpiān bù tīng wǒ de huà.
examples.english: You just insist on not listening to me.

components.note: 攵 (tap, hand with stick) — acts that direct others: 教 teach, 放 release, 改 change, 收 collect; 政 is governing.
正 (zhèng) is the same sound; fits the sense too — government puts things right.
⺮ (bamboo) — marks bamboo and things made of it, as in 笔, 筷, 签; 策 was a bamboo whip or slip, then a plan.
朿 (cì) hints at the sound: 策 cè is close.

example.hanzi: 政府出台了新的环保政策。
example.pinyin: zhèngfǔ chūtái le xīn de huánbǎo zhèngcè.
example.english: The government introduced a new environmental policy.
example.fact: The 1987 Montreal Protocol, a global policy phasing out ozone-depleting chemicals, is considered one of the most successful environmental treaties ever. The ozone hole over Antarctica has been steadily shrinking since, and scientists project it could fully heal by around 2066.

examples.hanzi: 新的政策对小企业很有帮助。
examples.pinyin: Xīn de zhèngcè duì xiǎo qǐyè hěn yǒu bāngzhù.
examples.english: The new policy is very helpful to small businesses.

examples.hanzi: 学校的退款政策是什么？
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào de tuìkuǎn zhèngcè shì shénme?
examples.english: What is the school's refund policy?

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 指 is the finger or to point.
旨 (zhǐ) sounds exactly like 指; also in 脂 zhī.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — 责 first meant demanding payment of a debt, hence duty. 责 sounds out 债 zhài, 积 jī and 绩 jì.

example.hanzi: 他因为迟到而受到老板的指责。
example.pinyin: tā yīnwèi chídào ér shòudào lǎobǎn de zhǐzé.
example.english: He was criticized by his boss for being late.
example.fact: Galileo was formally denounced and placed under house arrest by the Roman Inquisition in 1633 for supporting the idea that Earth orbits the Sun. The Catholic Church did not formally acknowledge his findings were correct until 1992.

examples.hanzi: 别总是指责别人，先看看自己。
examples.pinyin: Bié zǒngshì zhǐzé biéren, xiān kànkan zìjǐ.
examples.english: Don't always blame others; look at yourself first.

examples.hanzi: 他的做法受到了大家的指责。
examples.pinyin: Tā de zuòfǎ shòudào le dàjiā de zhǐzé.
examples.english: His approach drew criticism from everyone.

components.note: 八 (eight) — originally two strokes pulling apart, meaning divide; that sense is in 分 divide, 公 public and 半 half.
卜 (divination) — the cracks read on heated bones; marks fortune-telling, as in 占 zhān to divine.
圭 (guī) is a loose sound clue; 挂 guà (to hang) shares this part and is exactly guà.

example.hanzi: 同事们喜欢在午休时聊八卦。
example.pinyin: tóngshìmen xǐhuān zài wǔxiū shí liáo bāguà.
example.english: Coworkers like to chat about gossip during lunch break.
example.fact: Studies of primate behavior suggest gossip-like social grooming and information-sharing may have evolved as a way for early humans to track alliances and reputations in growing social groups. Some anthropologists argue this social function was itself a major driver behind the evolution of complex communication.

examples.hanzi: 她最喜欢看明星八卦新闻。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuì xǐhuan kàn míngxīng bāguà xīnwén.
examples.english: She loves reading celebrity gossip the most.

examples.hanzi: 你怎么这么八卦，别问了。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zěnme zhème bāguà, bié wèn le.
examples.english: Why are you so nosy? Stop asking.

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water and liquids: 河, 汤, 洗; 汽 is steam, water turned to vapor.
气 (qì) is the same sound, and means vapor too.
氵 (water radical, 三点水) — marks liquids and things that flow, as in 河 river, 汤 soup, 酒 liquor; here an oily liquid.
由 (yóu) sounds exactly like 油 — the same sound clue appears in 邮 yóu and 柚 yòu.

example.hanzi: 车子的油箱里没有汽油了。
example.pinyin: chēzi de yóuxiāng lǐ méiyǒu qìyóu le.
example.english: There's no gasoline left in the car's tank.
example.fact: Gasoline is refined from crude oil through fractional distillation, which separates hydrocarbons by boiling point. A single barrel of crude oil yields only about 19 gallons of gasoline alongside diesel, jet fuel, and dozens of other refined products.

examples.hanzi: 这辆车每百公里要用八升汽油。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liàng chē měi bǎi gōnglǐ yào yòng bā shēng qìyóu.
examples.english: This car uses eight liters of gasoline per hundred kilometers.

examples.hanzi: 汽油最近又涨价了。
examples.pinyin: Qìyóu zuìjìn yòu zhǎngjià le.
examples.english: Gasoline prices went up again recently.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 哭 has two mouths 吅 wailing aloud; 口 marks mouth and voice words, as in 叫 shout, 唱 sing.
氵 (water) — the tears; also in 汗 sweat, 泪 tear.
立 (lì) is only a loose sound clue today, far from qì.

example.hanzi: 婴儿因为饿了而哭泣。
example.pinyin: yīng'ér yīnwèi è le ér kūqì.
example.english: The baby wept because it was hungry.
example.fact: Human emotional tears contain a different chemical composition than reflex tears caused by irritants like onions. They carry stress hormones and natural painkillers, leading some researchers to suggest crying may help the body regulate stress after intense emotion.

examples.hanzi: 她躲在房间里偷偷哭泣。
examples.pinyin: Tā duǒ zài fángjiān lǐ tōutōu kūqì.
examples.english: She hid in her room and wept quietly.

examples.hanzi: 听到哭泣声，妈妈马上跑了过去。
examples.pinyin: Tīngdào kūqì shēng, māma mǎshàng pǎo le guòqù.
examples.english: Hearing the sound of crying, Mom ran over at once.

components.note: 贝 (shell, money) — 贝 is money, as in 买, 费, 贵; 财 is wealth.
才 (cái) — same sound — 财 is cái, like 才; 才 also sounds out 材 cái.
宀 (roof) — a house, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 完; 富 is a house full of goods, hence rich.
畐 (fú) gives the sound: 富 fù is close, as in 福 fú and 副 fù.

example.hanzi: 他把大部分财富都捐给了慈善机构。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ dà bùfèn cáifù dōu juān gěi le císhàn jīgòu.
example.english: He donated most of his wealth to charity.
example.fact: Economists estimate that the wealthiest 1% of the global population holds nearly half of all household wealth worldwide. That concentration has been rising steadily since the 1980s, according to long-running World Inequality Database research.

examples.hanzi: 健康是人生最大的财富。
examples.pinyin: Jiànkāng shì rénshēng zuì dà de cáifù.
examples.english: Health is the greatest wealth in life.

examples.hanzi: 他靠自己的努力创造了大量财富。
examples.pinyin: Tā kào zìjǐ de nǔlì chuàngzào le dàliàng cáifù.
examples.english: He created a great deal of wealth through his own efforts.

components.note: 氵 (water) — liquids and flowing; 没 first meant sink or submerge (淹没), which led to "gone" and then "not have".
殳 (shū) is only a loose sound hint for 没 (méi/mò); it also sits in 设 shè and 投 tóu.
门 (gate) — a picture of a two-leaf door; as a radical it frames characters of doors and openings — 开, 关, 问, 间.

example.hanzi: 想让我借钱给你?没门!
example.pinyin: xiǎng ràng wǒ jiè qián gěi nǐ? méimén!
example.english: You want me to lend you money? No way!
example.fact: At the United Nations Security Council, any one of the five permanent members can single-handedly kill a resolution with a single "no" vote. That veto power has been exercised more than 300 times since 1946, more than half of them by the Soviet Union or Russia.

examples.hanzi: 想让我白干活？没门！
examples.pinyin: Xiǎng ràng wǒ bái gànhuó? Méimén!
examples.english: You want me to work for free? No way!

examples.hanzi: 他想插队？没门，请排好队。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng chāduì? Méimén, qǐng pái hǎo duì.
examples.english: He wants to cut in line? Not a chance; please queue up.

components.note: 日 (sun) — sun, light and time: 明 bright, 晴 clear, 时 time; stars are points of light.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint for xīng (-ng ending); also in 性 xìng, 姓 xìng.
月 (moon, month) — time and the moon: 明 bright, 朗 clear; in 期 it is a set period, as in 星期 week.
其 (qí) is the same sound with a different tone; also in 旗 qí, 棋 qí, 欺 qī.
大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.

example.hanzi: 我们星期天一起去爬山吧。
example.pinyin: wǒmen xīngqītiān yìqǐ qù páshān ba.
example.english: Let's go hiking together on Sunday.
example.fact: The seven-day week has no basis in astronomy — it originated with the ancient Babylonians, who linked each day to one of the seven visible "wandering" celestial bodies known at the time. Those were the Sun, Moon, and the five planets visible to the naked eye.

examples.hanzi: 星期天我通常在家休息。
examples.pinyin: Xīngqītiān wǒ tōngcháng zài jiā xiūxi.
examples.english: On Sundays I usually rest at home.

examples.hanzi: 下个星期天是我妈妈的生日。
examples.pinyin: Xià gè xīngqītiān shì wǒ māma de shēngrì.
examples.english: Next Sunday is my mom's birthday.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 偶 first meant a figure or doll, then a pair.
禺 (yú) is a loose sound clue; same part in 遇 yù, 愚 yú, 寓 yù.

example.hanzi: 他偶尔会来我家吃饭。
example.pinyin: Tā ǒu'ěr huì lái wǒ jiā chī fàn.
example.english: He occasionally comes to my house for dinner.
example.fact: 偶尔 means "once in a while" while 偶然 means "by chance." 偶 also means pairs: 偶数 (even numbers), 配偶 (spouse). And 偶像 (idol) and 木偶 (puppet) come from its older "figurine" sense.

examples.hanzi: 他是我的偶像。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de ǒuxiàng.
examples.english: He is my idol.

examples.hanzi: 这是一次偶然的机会。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí cì ǒurán de jīhuì.
examples.english: This was a chance opportunity.

components.note: 亻 (person) — an older kinsman; also in 他 he, 们 plural.
白 (bái) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 泊 bó and 柏 bǎi.

example.hanzi: 我伯伯是医生。
example.pinyin: Wǒ bóbo shì yīshēng.
example.english: My uncle is a doctor.
example.fact: Chinese kinship terms are precise: 伯伯 is your father's elder brother, 叔叔 his younger brother. 伯伯 can also be a polite address to an older man outside the family. 伯 is also the "earl" rank in the old five noble titles.

examples.hanzi: 我伯父住在上海。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bófù zhù zài Shànghǎi.
examples.english: My uncle lives in Shanghai.

examples.hanzi: 那位老伯伯在公园里下棋。
examples.pinyin: Nà wèi lǎo bóbo zài gōngyuán li xià qí.
examples.english: That old gentleman is playing chess in the park.

components.note: 亻 (person, 单人旁) — marks people and relationships, as in 他 he, 们 plural, 住 live.
至 (zhì) nearly matches zhí, with a different tone; it also sounds out 致 zhì and 室 shì.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 我的侄子今年上大学了。
example.pinyin: wǒ de zhízi jīnnián shàng dàxué le.
example.english: My nephew started college this year.
example.fact: Napoleon Bonaparte's nephew, Napoleon III, later became the first president of France and then its last monarch, ruling as emperor until 1870. They are one of history's few uncle-nephew pairs to each independently seize supreme power over the same country.

examples.hanzi: 我的侄子特别喜欢踢足球。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de zhízi tèbié xǐhuan tī zúqiú.
examples.english: My nephew really loves playing football.

examples.hanzi: 周末我带侄子去了动物园。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ dài zhízi qù le dòngwùyuán.
examples.english: At the weekend I took my nephew to the zoo.

components.note: 氺 (water, a variant of 水) — the old form has water below hands and a big person above: calm, great, secure. Same character in 泰国 Thailand.
大 (big) — top of the character. Memory aid: a big (大) volume of water held steady is calm and 'great'.
革 (leather) — marks hides and straps, as in 鞋, 靴 boots, 鞭 whip; 勒 is to rein in or tighten.
力 (lì) is only a loose sound hint for lè.

example.hanzi: 泰勒是我们班新来的交换生。
example.pinyin: Tàilè shì wǒmen bān xīn lái de jiāohuàn shēng.
example.english: Taylor is the new exchange student in our class.
example.fact: The English surname Taylor derives from the medieval occupation of tailoring. It remains one of the most common English surnames precisely because clothing production was one of the largest trades in pre-industrial Europe, alongside names like Smith and Mason.

examples.hanzi: 泰勒每天骑自行车去学校。
examples.pinyin: Tàilè měi tiān qí zìxíngchē qù xuéxiào.
examples.english: Taylor rides a bike to school every day.

examples.hanzi: 我昨天和泰勒一起吃了午饭。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān hé Tàilè yìqǐ chī le wǔfàn.
examples.english: I had lunch with Taylor yesterday.

components.note: 良 (liáng) — good; as a part it sounds out 粮 liáng, 狼 láng, 浪 làng and 朗 lǎng.
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.hanzi: 他的良心让他说出了实话。
example.pinyin: tā de liángxīn ràng tā shuō chū le shíhuà.
example.english: His conscience made him tell the truth.
example.fact: Phineas Gage, a 19th-century railway worker who survived a tamping iron piercing his skull in 1848, reportedly underwent a dramatic personality change afterward. The case became an early study that helped scientists link the brain's frontal lobe to moral judgment and impulse control.

examples.hanzi: 做生意要讲良心，不能骗人。
examples.pinyin: Zuò shēngyi yào jiǎng liángxīn, bù néng piàn rén.
examples.english: In business you should have a conscience and not cheat people.

examples.hanzi: 你这样做，良心过得去吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhèyàng zuò, liángxīn guò de qù ma?
examples.english: Can you live with yourself doing it this way?

components.note: 犬 (dog) — a sacrifice was offered with a dog, hence 献 is to present or offer; the left side is a simplified stand-in.

example.hanzi: 他把一生献给了教育事业。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ yìshēng xiàn gěi le jiàoyù shìyè.
example.english: He dedicated his whole life to education.
example.fact: 献 is a formal way to give: 献花 (present flowers), 献血 (donate blood), 献礼 (offer a tribute), 贡献 (contribution). Compared with the everyday 送, 献 implies respect, devotion, or a solemn occasion.

examples.hanzi: 他向医院献了一次血。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiàng yīyuàn xiàn le yí cì xuè.
examples.english: He donated blood to the hospital once.

examples.hanzi: 他为社会作出了很大的贡献。
examples.pinyin: Tā wèi shèhuì zuòchū le hěn dà de gòngxiàn.
examples.english: He made a great contribution to society.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 叶 is a leaf (simplified from 葉); in the older sense xié it means to harmonise.

example.hanzi: 秋天到了，树叶都黄了。
example.pinyin: Qiūtiān dào le, shùyè dōu huáng le.
example.english: Autumn has come and the leaves have all turned yellow.
example.fact: 叶 is the simplified form of 葉. The simplification borrowed an existing old character 叶 (xié, "harmonize"), so one glyph now serves for "leaf." It is also a surname in the form 叶, and the word is 叶子 or 树叶.

examples.hanzi: 这片叶子很大。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piàn yèzi hěn dà.
examples.english: This leaf is very big.

examples.hanzi: 他把茶叶放进杯子里。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ cháyè fàng jìn bēizi li.
examples.english: He put tea leaves into the cup.

components.note: 公 (public) — 八 over 厶: dividing 八 what is private 厶; so "shared, public, fair".

example.hanzi: 我每天坐公共汽车去上班。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān zuò gōnggòng qìchē qù shàngbān.
example.english: I take the bus to work every day.
example.fact: 公 has two big branches: "public/fair" (公平, 公园, 公司) and "male" for animals (公鸡 rooster, 公牛 bull), opposed to 母. In measures, 公 is the metric prefix: 公里 (kilometre), 公斤 (kilogram).

examples.hanzi: 这家公司在上海。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī zài Shànghǎi.
examples.english: This company is in Shanghai.

examples.hanzi: 公平一点,别偏心。
examples.pinyin: Gōngpíng yìdiǎn, bié piānxīn.
examples.english: Be fair; don't play favorites.

components.note: 舛 (two opposed feet) — the dancer's footwork; 無 (wú) above is a loose sound clue, as it once meant dance itself.
止 (foot) — two footprints, one above the other, make a step; the same 止 is in 走 walk and 跑 run.

example.hanzi: 她练习了很多遍探戈的舞步。
example.pinyin: tā liànxí le hěn duō biàn tàngē de wǔbù.
example.english: She practiced the tango's dance steps many times over.
example.fact: Tango originated in the working-class port neighborhoods of Buenos Aires and Montevideo in the late 1800s, blending African, European, and South American musical traditions. It was initially considered scandalous and was banned from some European ballrooms when it first arrived around 1913.

examples.hanzi: 老师教我们跳一种简单的舞步。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī jiāo wǒmen tiào yì zhǒng jiǎndān de wǔbù.
examples.english: The teacher taught us a simple dance step.

examples.hanzi: 他的舞步很轻快，大家都在看他。
examples.pinyin: Tā de wǔbù hěn qīngkuài, dàjiā dōu zài kàn tā.
examples.english: His dance steps were light and lively, and everyone was watching him.

components.note: 水 (water) — water and flow: 永 first meant a long river. 泳 yǒng (swimming) added the water radical later.
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.

example.hanzi: 她发誓永不放弃自己的梦想。
example.pinyin: tā fāshì yǒngbù fàngqì zìjǐ de mèngxiǎng.
example.english: She swore she would never give up on her dream.
example.fact: Voyager 1, launched in 1977, is now over 15 billion miles from Earth and will likely keep drifting through interstellar space forever. Its power will run out around 2025, but the probe itself is destined to outlast our planet.

examples.hanzi: 我永不会忘记你对我的帮助。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒng bú huì wàngjì nǐ duì wǒ de bāngzhù.
examples.english: I will never forget the help you gave me.

examples.hanzi: 他们约定永不分离。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen yuēdìng yǒng bù fēnlí.
examples.english: They promised never to be apart.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室: a building holds things.
谷 (valley) — a hollow that holds: 容 is to hold or allow.
心 (heart) — 心 is the heart, as in 想, 思, 念; 忍 is a blade 刃 over the heart — enduring pain.
刃 (rèn) — near sound — 忍 is rěn; 刃 is a blade with an edge marked by a dot.

example.hanzi: 老师容忍了学生的一些小错误。
example.pinyin: lǎoshī róngrěn le xuésheng de yìxiē xiǎo cuòwù.
example.english: The teacher tolerated some of the students' small mistakes.
example.fact: Coral reefs can tolerate only a narrow temperature range — a sustained rise of just 1-2°C above normal summer maximums triggers mass bleaching. This has occurred across large sections of Australia's Great Barrier Reef during repeated marine heatwaves since 2016.

examples.hanzi: 我不能容忍有人在会上玩手机。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù néng róngrěn yǒu rén zài huì shàng wán shǒujī.
examples.english: I can't tolerate people playing with their phones in meetings.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈对孩子的任性已经容忍很久了。
examples.pinyin: Māma duì háizi de rènxìng yǐjīng róngrěn hěn jiǔ le.
examples.english: Mom has put up with her child's willfulness for a long time.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 嗑 is cracking seeds with the teeth, as in 嗑瓜子.
盍 (hé) — loose sound hint (kè vs hé).

example.hanzi: 他喜欢一边看电视一边嗑瓜子。
example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan yìbiān kàn diànshì yìbiān kè guāzǐ.
example.english: He likes to crack sunflower seeds while watching TV.
example.fact: 嗑瓜子 is a classic snack habit in China, especially at Spring Festival. Online, 嗑 has gained a slang sense: 嗑CP means to enjoy a fictional or celebrity couple, savoring the pairing like a snack.

examples.hanzi: 过年时,大家边聊天边嗑瓜子。
examples.pinyin: Guònián shí, dàjiā biān liáotiān biān kè guāzǐ.
examples.english: At New Year, everyone cracks sunflower seeds while chatting.

examples.hanzi: 小松鼠在嗑松子。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo sōngshǔ zài kè sōngzǐ.
examples.english: The little squirrel is gnawing pine nuts.

components.note: 周 (zhōu) also lends its sound to 调 diào/tiáo, 稠 chóu, 绸 chóu and 凋 diāo.
日 (sun, day) — a picture of the sun, once round with a dot, now squared off. As a radical it marks light and time: 明, 晴, 时.

example.hanzi: 他周日要去医院复查。
example.pinyin: tā zhōurì yào qù yīyuàn fùchá.
example.english: He needs to go back to the hospital for a checkup on Sunday.
example.fact: The Gregorian calendar's seven-day week has no astronomical basis — it traces back to ancient Babylon's fascination with seven visible celestial bodies (the sun, moon, and five planets). The Romans later spread the practice empire-wide, and it survived the fall of Rome to become the near-universal standard in use today.

examples.hanzi: 周日我们一家人去爬山。
examples.pinyin: Zhōurì wǒmen yījiārén qù páshān.
examples.english: On Sunday our whole family goes hiking.

examples.hanzi: 这家店周日不营业。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn zhōurì bù yíngyè.
examples.english: This shop is closed on Sundays.

meanings: (slang) to fail to catch anything (on a fishing trip)

components.note: 穴 (cave) — 穴 is a cave or hole, as in 窗 window, 穷 poor; 空 is empty like a hollow.
工 (gōng) — near sound — 空 is kōng; also in 红 hóng.
车 (chariot) — war chariots drawn up in a circle (the top part shows the enclosure): an army camp, hence military.

example.hanzi: 他的梦想是加入空军,成为一名飞行员。
example.pinyin: tā de mèngxiǎng shì jiārù kōngjūn, chéngwéi yī míng fēixíngyuán.
example.english: His dream is to join the air force and become a pilot.
example.fact: The Royal Air Force, founded in 1918, was the world's first air force established as a fully independent military branch, separate from the army and navy. Most other nations' air forces grew directly out of army aviation corps and only became independent services decades later.

examples.hanzi: 他在空军服役了八年。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài kōngjūn fúyì le bā nián.
examples.english: He served in the air force for eight years.

examples.hanzi: 空军的飞机从头顶飞过。
examples.pinyin: Kōngjūn de fēijī cóng tóudǐng fēiguò.
examples.english: Air force planes flew overhead.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and roles: 你, 他, 位; 使 is sending someone to do something.
吏 (lì, official) gives the meaning, and shares its ancestor 史 (shǐ), the exact sound of 使.
彳 (step) — walking and going, as in 行, 往, 很 very.
寸 (hand) — oldest form is a hand grabbing a cowrie shell (money): 得 is "to obtain". The shell has worn down to 旦.

example.hanzi: 长期缺水使得这片土地变成了沙漠。
example.pinyin: chángqī quēshuǐ shǐde zhè piàn tǔdì biànchéngle shāmò.
example.english: Long-term water scarcity caused this land to turn into a desert.
example.fact: The Aral Sea, once the world's fourth-largest lake, has shrunk by over 90% since the 1960s after Soviet irrigation projects diverted the rivers feeding it. Vast stretches of the former lakebed are now a new desert called the Aralkum, visible from space.

examples.hanzi: 这个办法使得工作更轻松了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bànfǎ shǐde gōngzuò gèng qīngsōng le.
examples.english: This method has made the work easier.

examples.hanzi: 下雨使得比赛推迟了。
examples.pinyin: Xiàyǔ shǐde bǐsài tuīchí le.
examples.english: The rain caused the match to be postponed.

components.note: 上 (above) — 上 over 下 squeezed together: something stuck in the middle, the sense of qiǎ (to wedge); kǎ is the borrowed sound for "card" and "car", as in 信用卡 and 卡车.
片 (slice) — the right half of 木 split down the middle: a flat piece. See 版 bǎn (printing plate) and 牌 pái (card).

example.hanzi: 她在生日卡片上写了一句祝福的话。
example.pinyin: tā zài shēngrì kǎpiàn shàng xiěle yī jù zhùfú de huà.
example.english: She wrote a blessing on the birthday card.
example.fact: The world's oldest surviving printed book, the Diamond Sutra from Dunhuang, China, was produced in AD 868 using woodblock printing — over five centuries before Gutenberg's press appeared in Europe.

examples.hanzi: 我收到了一张朋友寄来的卡片。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shōudào le yī zhāng péngyou jìlái de kǎpiàn.
examples.english: I received a card sent by a friend.

examples.hanzi: 请把名字写在这张卡片上。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ míngzi xiě zài zhè zhāng kǎpiàn shàng.
examples.english: Please write your name on this card.

components.note: 月 (flesh) — ⺼ is the body radical (月 in 脸, 脑); 脱 is slipping off a layer, like skin or clothes.
兑 (duì) — near sound — 脱 is tuō; 兑 also sounds out 说 shuō and 税 shuì.
衣 (clothes) — a picture of a coat with a collar and sleeves. As a radical it is 衤 on the left: 裤 trousers, 衬 shirt, 被 quilt.
舛 (two opposed feet) — the dancer's footwork; 無 (wú) above is a loose sound clue, as it once meant dance itself.

example.hanzi: 那家夜店表演脱衣舞,吸引了不少游客。
example.pinyin: nà jiā yèdiàn biǎoyǎn tuōyīwǔ, xīyǐnle bùshǎo yóukè.
example.english: That nightclub performs striptease shows, attracting many tourists.
example.fact: Burlesque striptease as an American stage art traces back to the 1860s, when touring British troupes blended satire, comedy, and daring costume into a new form of variety theater — decades before it became associated with Las Vegas showmanship in the 20th century.

examples.hanzi: 我们没有去看脱衣舞表演。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen méiyǒu qù kàn tuōyīwǔ biǎoyǎn.
examples.english: We didn't go to see the striptease show.

examples.hanzi: 这家酒吧晚上有脱衣舞。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā jiǔbā wǎnshang yǒu tuōyīwǔ.
examples.english: This bar has a striptease act in the evening.
